title: Typeform vs Formbricks
comparison_markdown:
# Typeform vs Formbricks

## Overview

Conversational form and survey tool known for its beautiful, interactive design. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. Formbricks is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Typeform costs Free / $25-$83/month; Formbricks is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Typeform is Proprietary; Formbricks is AGPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: Formbricks can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Formbricks eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Formbricks has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Typeform | Formbricks |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $25-$83/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Typeform

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Formbricks

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [formbricks/formbricks](https://github.com/formbricks/formbricks) * ~9k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Typeform if:** Typeform is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Formbricks if:** Formbricks is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Typeform in its standard export format, review Formbricks import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Formbricks is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Typeform tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Formbricks instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Typeform, switching to self-hosted Formbricks will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Typeform until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Typeform paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Formbricks free to use?
Yes. Formbricks is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Typeform to Formbricks?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Typeform data, follow the Formbricks import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Formbricks get regular updates?
Yes. Formbricks has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Formbricks without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Formbricks development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced May 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Typeform](https://typeform.com) and [Formbricks](https://formbricks.com) before making decisions.*

# Miro vs Excalidraw (2026)

## Overview
Miro and Excalidraw are two popular tools used for collaborative whiteboarding and visual communication. This comparison is beneficial for teams and individuals who rely on these tools for brainstorming, project planning, and design. The core use case for both tools is to facilitate remote collaboration and idea sharing, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data or reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Miro offers a free plan and several paid plans, while Excalidraw is completely free.
* Data Ownership: Excalidraw allows users to self-host their data, giving them full control over their content, whereas Miro stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup Complexity: Excalidraw requires more technical expertise to set up, especially for self-hosting, while Miro is generally easier to get started with.
* Scalability: Miro is designed to handle large teams and enterprises, while Excalidraw is better suited for smaller teams and individuals.
* Integration: Miro has a wider range of integrations with popular tools like Google Drive and Trello, while Excalidraw has limited integrations but is highly customizable.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Miro | Excalidraw |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $8-$16/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $400-$800/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,600-$3,200/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
Miro Pros:
* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of integrations
* Scalable for large teams
* Robust collaboration features
* Good customer support
Miro Cons:
* Limited control over data
* Can be expensive for large teams
* Limited customization options
* Proprietary license
* Limited self-hosting options
Excalidraw Pros:
* Completely free
* Self-hosting available
* Highly customizable
* Open-source license
* Full control over data
Excalidraw Cons:
* Steeper learning curve
* Limited integrations
* May require technical expertise to set up
* Limited support for large teams
* Limited collaboration features

## When to Choose Each
Miro is a good choice for large teams and enterprises that require a scalable and easy-to-use collaboration tool. It's also a good option for teams that don't mind paying a premium for a proprietary tool with good customer support. Excalidraw, on the other hand, is a good choice for smaller teams and individuals who value control over their data and customization options. It's also a good option for teams with technical expertise who can handle the setup and maintenance of a self-hosted solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Miro boards as JSON files using the Miro API or a third-party tool.
2. Set up an Excalidraw server using the official documentation and your preferred hosting method.
3. Use the Excalidraw import tool to import your Miro boards into Excalidraw.
4. Configure any necessary settings and customize your Excalidraw instance to fit your team's needs.
5. Test your Excalidraw instance to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Excalidraw is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the polish and features of Miro. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Excalidraw's self-hosting option requires a good amount of technical expertise to set up and maintain. However, for teams that value control over their data and customization options, Excalidraw is a good choice, and we recommend switching from Miro to Excalidraw if you're a small team or individual with technical expertise.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who don't need advanced collaboration features
* Individuals who value control over their data and customization options
* Teams with technical expertise who can handle self-hosting and maintenance
* Teams who are currently using Miro's free plan and need more features
* Teams who are looking for a cost-effective solution and don't mind a steeper learning curve

## FAQ
### Can I use Excalidraw for free?
Yes, Excalidraw is completely free, with no limits on users or features.
### Is Excalidraw self-hosting available?
Yes, Excalidraw offers self-hosting options, giving you full control over your data.
### Can I import my Miro boards into Excalidraw?
Yes, you can import your Miro boards into Excalidraw using the Excalidraw import tool.
### Does Excalidraw have good customer support?
Excalidraw has limited customer support, but it's an open-source project with an active community.
### Can I use Excalidraw for large teams?
Excalidraw is not yet suitable for large teams, as it lacks some of the scalability and collaboration features of Miro.

title: Netlify vs Coolify

# Netlify vs Coolify (2026)

## Overview
Netlify and Coolify are two popular tools used for building, deploying, and managing modern web applications. This comparison is beneficial for developers and teams looking to choose between a proprietary, cloud-based platform (Netlify) and a self-hosted, open-source alternative (Coolify). The core use case for both tools is to streamline the development and deployment process, and a key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and infrastructure.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Netlify offers a free plan and paid plans starting at $19/month, while Coolify is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Coolify allows users to retain full ownership and control over their data, whereas Netlify stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Netlify is generally easier to set up, with a more user-friendly interface, while Coolify requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Netlify offers automatic scaling and load balancing, while Coolify requires manual configuration.
* Feature difference: Netlify has built-in support for serverless functions, while Coolify requires additional setup for similar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Netlify | Coolify |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $19-$99/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $19-$99/month (depending on plan) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $99-$499/month (depending on plan) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Netlify:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Automatic scaling and load balancing
* Built-in support for serverless functions
* Large community and good documentation
* Limited control over data and infrastructure
**Coolify:**
* Self-hosted and open-source
* Full control over data and infrastructure
* Customizable and extensible
* Free and cost-effective
* Steeper learning curve and more complex setup

## When to Choose Each
Netlify is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams that prioritize ease of use and don't require fine-grained control over their infrastructure. It's also suitable for projects that require built-in support for serverless functions and automatic scaling. On the other hand, Coolify is a better fit for larger teams or organizations that require more control over their data and infrastructure, and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining their own servers.

## Migration Path
1. Export your site and data from Netlify using their export tool, which generates a ZIP file containing your site's code and data.
2. Set up a new Coolify instance on your own server, using a tool like Docker or a virtual machine.
3. Import your site and data into Coolify using their import tool, which supports ZIP files exported from Netlify.
4. Configure any additional settings or integrations required by Coolify, such as setting up a new domain or configuring serverless functions.
5. Test your site and data to ensure a smooth transition.

## Our Take
Coolify is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires significant technical expertise to set up and maintain. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Coolify currently lacks built-in support for serverless functions, which may be a deal-breaker for some users. However, for teams that require more control over their data and infrastructure, and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining their own servers, Coolify is a viable alternative to Netlify.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams that don't require built-in support for serverless functions and want more control over their data and infrastructure
* Medium-sized teams that are currently using Netlify's free plan and want to avoid paying for additional features
* Large teams that require fine-grained control over their infrastructure and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining their own servers
* Teams that prioritize data ownership and want to self-host their applications
* Developers who want a customizable and extensible platform for building and deploying their applications

## FAQ
### What is the main difference between Netlify and Coolify?
The main difference between Netlify and Coolify is that Netlify is a proprietary, cloud-based platform, while Coolify is a self-hosted, open-source alternative. This means that with Coolify, you have full control over your data and infrastructure, but you also need to manage and maintain your own servers.
### Is Coolify free?
Yes, Coolify is free and open-source. However, you will need to pay for your own server costs if you choose to self-host.
### Can I use Coolify for large-scale applications?
Yes, Coolify can be used for large-scale applications, but it requires more technical expertise and resources to set up and maintain.
### Does Coolify support serverless functions?
No, Coolify currently lacks built-in support for serverless functions, which may be a limitation for some users.
### Is Coolify production-ready?
No, Coolify is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires significant technical expertise to set up and maintain.

* Cost: Shopify has a monthly subscription fee, while WooCommerce is free to download and use.
* Data ownership: Shopify stores data on its servers, while WooCommerce allows users to host their data on their own servers.
* Setup complexity: Shopify has a more streamlined setup process, while WooCommerce requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: Shopify has built-in scalability features, while WooCommerce requires third-party plugins to scale.
* Payment gateways: Shopify has a limited number of payment gateways, while WooCommerce supports over 200 payment gateways through extensions.

| Aspect | Shopify | WooCommerce |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $29-$299+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $29-$299+/month (flat fee) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $29-$299+/month (flat fee) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Shopify:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Scalable and secure
* 24/7 customer support
* Limited customization options
* Transaction fees apply
**WooCommerce:**
* Free to download and use
* Highly customizable
* Large community of developers and users
* Requires technical expertise to set up and use
* Limited customer support

## When to Choose Each
Shopify is ideal for small to medium-sized businesses that want a hassle-free e-commerce solution with built-in scalability and security features. It's perfect for teams with limited technical expertise who want to focus on selling products rather than managing their website. On the other hand, WooCommerce is suitable for large enterprises or businesses with complex e-commerce requirements that need a high degree of customization and control over their data. It's ideal for teams with technical expertise who want to host their own servers and have complete control over their online store.

## Migration Path
1. Export your products, customers, and orders from Shopify using the CSV export feature.
2. Install the WooCommerce plugin on your WordPress website and set up the basic configuration.
3. Use the WooCommerce import tool to import your products, customers, and orders from the CSV file.
4. Configure any additional settings, such as payment gateways and shipping options.
5. Test your website to ensure everything is working correctly.

## Our Take
WooCommerce is a production-ready e-commerce platform for most users, offering a high degree of customization and control over data. However, one technical limitation worth knowing is that WooCommerce requires a compatible theme to function properly, which can be a challenge for users without technical expertise. Based on our analysis, we recommend switching to WooCommerce if you're a small to medium-sized business with technical expertise and want more control over your data, but if you're a large enterprise with complex e-commerce requirements, Shopify may still be the better choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 employees who don't need built-in scalability features
* Medium-sized businesses with 10-50 employees who want more control over their data
* Enterprises with over 100 employees who have technical expertise and want to host their own servers
* Businesses that don't need 24/7 customer support
* Teams with limited budget who want a free e-commerce solution

No, WooCommerce requires a compatible theme to function properly.

Yes, WooCommerce supports over 200 payment gateways through extensions.
### Is WooCommerce suitable for large enterprises?
Yes, WooCommerce can be suitable for large enterprises with complex e-commerce requirements, but it requires technical expertise and proper configuration.

# Sentry vs GlitchTip (2026)

## Overview
Sentry and GlitchTip are error tracking and monitoring tools that help developers identify and resolve issues in their applications. This comparison is beneficial for development teams looking to choose between a proprietary and an open-source solution, with a key reason to switch being the desire for greater control over their data and costs. The core use case for both tools is to provide insights into application errors, allowing teams to improve their overall quality and user experience.

* Cost: Sentry offers a free plan with limited features, while GlitchTip is free and open-source, with costs limited to self-hosting.
* Data ownership: GlitchTip allows for full data ownership since it can be self-hosted, whereas Sentry stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Sentry is generally easier to set up, with a more streamlined onboarding process, while GlitchTip requires more technical expertise for self-hosting.
* Scalability: Sentry is designed to handle large volumes of data and traffic, while GlitchTip's scalability depends on the self-hosting infrastructure.
* Integration with GitHub: Sentry has native integration with GitHub, while GlitchTip supports GitHub integration through its API.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Sentry | GlitchTip |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $26-$80+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | BSD |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $26-$40/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |

On the other hand, GlitchTip is a good choice for teams that value control over their data, customization, and cost-effectiveness, and are willing to invest time and expertise into self-hosting and setup. * Small teams (less than 10 users) that do not need native integration with GitHub and prioritize cost-effectiveness.
